The Practice — where Zia stands

Zia ran as an in-home and video practice from at least January 2020, then opened its first brick-and-mortar clinic in Merrifield on 2 September 2026. The positioning is sharp — performance-driven pelvic health and orthopedics for active women, “No referral needed” — but the public footprint hasn't caught up with the clinic yet.

1 · We swept everything public

Website, Instagram, directories, podcasts, events and competitors — baked in with sources, dated 5 Nov 2026.

2 · Sara fills in what only she knows

Revenue, visits, bookings, review counts — the Update tab turns her answers into a packet she downloads or emails back. Nothing is stored on this page.

3 · We sweep again and refresh

Her packet plus a fresh public sweep updates this same page at this same link.

Pelvic health — what Zia treats

  • Bladder & bowel — leakage, urgency, frequency, constipation, bladder pain
  • Pregnancy & postpartum — birth prep and recovery, diastasis recti, C-section / perineal scar pain, return to sport
  • Pelvic pain — endometriosis, pain with intimacy, vulvodynia, tailbone pain
  • Prolapse — including functional pessary fittings, a service few competitors advertise this explicitly

Orthopedics & performance

  • Low back, hip and SI-joint pain; knee pain; post-surgical care
  • Running gait analysis (RunEasi sensor system) + performance programming
  • Performance bike fittings for cyclists and triathletes
  • Return-to-sport and overuse-injury care

The Zia Blueprint: Break it Down → Balance the System → Build Capacity → Be Resilient. Open question: dry needling is not listed on the current site, though Dr. Black holds a 2018 Functional Dry Needling Level I credential (provider-listed).

What patients say — owned testimonials, trapped on her own site

Recurring themes on ziapphysio.com/testimonials: never rushed or dismissed (“I never felt rushed or dismissed” — Luisa H.), prenatal-to-postpartum continuity (Giselle B.), return to running (Jose; Gretchen), and complex pelvic pain resolved after dismissal elsewhere (Pauline; Ethan, ~4 months post-surgical). A Qualtrics patient survey is also running — its quotes appear on Instagram, but none of it flows to Google, where prospects actually look.

Market context — directional only

Vendor estimates for pelvic-floor physiotherapy disagree wildly ($1.08B–$3.2B for 2025), but all agree postpartum, menopause/aging and prolapse awareness drive demand — exactly Zia's three pillars. Cash-PT industry data (PT Biz, 2025) puts continuity/wellness visits at 20–40%+ of volume at mature clinics; Zia publishes no package, membership or continuity offer.

Gap 1 · Highest leverage

Turn the Qualtrics survey into Google reviews

Satisfaction is already being measured — it's just hand-turned into Instagram quote cards while Google shows nothing. Adding one “review us on Google” step to the existing survey flow is the lowest-effort fix in this entire report.

Gap 2

Publish the money answer

No prices, no insurance position, and the FAQ never even asks the question — while PelviCore, Applied Performance and MovementX all answer it on-page. Every prospect is forced into a phone call. Open question for Sara — see the update form.

Gap 3

Replace the placeholder blog

Four 2020 template posts are the whole content library. The Mind Your Midlife topics (perimenopause, GLP-1s, bladder diary) are ready-made, searchable articles — and Casey + agency support (Luminy) already exist to produce them.

Gap 4

Capture event interest on her own list

Five events in six weeks ran on three different systems — Instagram DMs, Eventbrite/Mamistad, and walk-in (“just show up” = zero contacts captured). One owned RSVP + follow-up flow fixes the funnel she's already filling.

Gap 5

Listings hygiene — quick wins

  • Hours conflict: website says Mon–Fri 8–6; a Facebook-mirror directory says Mon–Thu 7–3:30. Which is right is unverified.
  • Vienna Business Association + Bornbir still list the old Dunn Loring address; WellnessLiving carries a stale, unclaimed “Arlington” listing.
  • Name order flips between “Zia Performance + Physiotherapy” and “ZIA Physiotherapy + Performance.”
  • Two typos on the most-visited pages: “Competitive Triathelete” and “physical therpy.”
  • The Triathlete Project site still sells the old in-home model.
